title_en: Xiangcai Securities Co., Ltd. v. China Everbright Bank, Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch, and Third Party: Hunan Ping'an Light Chemical Technology Industry Co., Ltd. — dispute over subrogation rights under a loan contract
ruling_gist_en: First, a contract between a client and a securities business institution, under which the client delivers funds to the securities business institution, entrusts the securities business institution to invest in the securities market within a certain period, and the securities business institution periodically pays investment returns to the client, constitutes an entrusted wealth management contract.

full_text_en:
Xiangcai Securities Co., Ltd. v. China Everbright Bank

Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch, Third Party Hunan Ping'an

Light Chemical Technology Industrial Co., Ltd.

— dispute over subrogation in a loan contract

【Ruling Summary】

1. Where a client enters into a contract with a securities operation institution, agreeing to entrust funds to the institution for investment in the securities market within a specified period, with the institution periodically paying investment returns to the client, such a contract constitutes a discretionary investment management contract.

2. Where the client and the securities operation institution agree in the discretionary investment management contract that the institution shall guarantee the client's investment return reaching a certain percentage, with the institution making up any shortfall, such an agreement constitutes a guaranteed minimum return clause, i.e., a guaranteed floor clause. Pursuant to Article 143 of the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China, securities firms shall not promise clients any returns on securities transactions or compensation for losses from securities transactions in any manner. The aforesaid guaranteed floor clause is invalid for violating this provision. Because the guaranteed floor clause is a purpose clause or core clause of the discretionary investment management contract, its invalidity renders the entire contract invalid.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2006) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 90

Appellant (original defendant): Xiangcai Securities Co., Ltd., domiciled at 12th Floor, Zhongshan International Building, No. 63 Huangxing Middle Road, Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Xuerong, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yi Hao, employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Yang Yue, lawyer of Hunan Chenbang Law Firm.

Appellee (original plaintiff): China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch, domiciled at No. 536 Furong North Road, Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Responsible Person: Wang Mingxiang, President of the sub-branch.

Agent ad litem: Zhou Wei, employee of the sub-branch.

Agent ad litem: Xiao Jianxiong, lawyer of Hunan Tiandiren Law Firm.

Original third party: Hunan Ping'an Light Chemical Technology Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 308 Licheng Road, Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Long Dahai, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Hu Mengqiang, lawyer of Hunan Hualin Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Tang Zhengyu, lawyer of Hunan Jiajing Law Firm.

The appellant Xiangcai Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xiangcai Securities), in a dispute with the appellee China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch) and the original third party Hunan Ping'an Light Chemical Technology Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ping'an Light Chemical) over subrogation in a loan contract, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2005) Xiang Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 14 of the Hunan High People's Court, appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Jin Jianfeng, Judge Chen Bailing, and Acting Judge Yang Zhengyu to hear the case, with Court Clerk Yuan Hongxia recording the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts after trial: Ping'an Light Chemical (Party A), Xiangcai Securities (Party B), and China Everbright Bank Changsha Branch (hereinafter referred to as Everbright Changsha Branch) (Party C) signed the "Sunshine Wealth Management Guarantee Agreement" on April 19, 2004, which stipulated: Whereas Party A agrees to entrust Party B to conduct discretionary investment management on behalf of Party A and has signed the "Discretionary Investment Management Contract," Party B applies to Party C for providing certain guarantees for the discretionary investment management business to ensure that Party A can obtain the ending balance of entrusted investment assets upon expiration of the "Discretionary Investment Management Contract"; Party C agrees to accept Party B's application. After full consultation among the three parties, they agree that Party C will provide sunshine wealth management guarantee business for the discretionary investment management business of Party A and Party B; Party C's guarantee amount is the ending asset balance of the entrusted assets under the "Discretionary Investment Management Contract"; the guarantee liability period is from the effective date of this agreement until the date the guarantee liability is discharged.

On April 21, 2004, Ping'an Light Chemical (Party A) and Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch (Party B) signed a "Loan Contract," agreeing: Party A borrows RMB 80 million from Party B for operational turnover, with a loan term from April 21, 2004 to October 21, 2004, an annual interest rate of 4.536%; overdue interest shall be charged at 0.0189% per day on the overdue amount, and compound interest on overdue interest shall be calculated at 0.0189% per day based on the overdue days. Ping'an Light Chemical provided the "Sunshine Wealth Management Guarantee Agreement" as a pledge to secure the above loan, and signed a pledge contract on April 21, 2004.

After the "Loan Contract" was signed, Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch transferred the loan to Ping'an Light Chemical's account 087881120100302012300 as agreed. On April 21, 2004, Ping'an Light Chemical and Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch signed a "Bank Acceptance Agreement" and issued eight bank acceptance drafts totaling RMB 80 million from the above account, which were accepted to FAW Trading Corporation and FAW Jiefang Qingdao Automobile Factory respectively.

Upon maturity of the "Loan Contract," Ping'an Light Chemical only repaid the interest during the contract period of RMB 1,542,240. As of October 21, 2004, the outstanding principal was RMB 80 million, with overdue principal interest of RMB 312,480, overdue interest of RMB 3,659,040, and compound interest of RMB 65,976.89, totaling principal of RMB 80 million and interest of RMB 4,037,496.89, for a total of RMB 84,037,496.89.

On April 20, 2004, Ping'an Light Chemical (Principal) and Xiangcai Securities (Agent) signed a "Discretionary Investment Management Contract," agreeing: The Principal delivers RMB 100 million to the Agent for investment management, with a management term commencing from the date the entrusted assets arrive in the Principal's discretionary investment management account and the Principal effectively authorizes the Agent to manage the account, lasting 12 months; during the management term, a discretionary investment management account shall be opened in the Principal's name by opening securities and fund accounts; the settlement method is cash settlement; both parties also agreed on management fees and performance bonuses. On the same day, the parties signed a "Supplementary Agreement," stipulating: The Agent guarantees the safety and integrity of the entrusted investment management assets, ensuring the annual investment return rate of the entrusted investment management assets reaches 7.8%; if the annual return rate is lower than 7.8%, the Agent shall make up the shortfall. The Agent agrees to pay the Principal RMB 1.95 million in returns on July 30, 2004, October 30, 2004, and January 30, 2005, respectively, and on the maturity date, transfer the remaining returns and principal to the Principal. Any returns on the entrusted investment management assets exceeding an annual rate of 7.8% shall be retained by the Agent as performance bonuses. On the same day, the parties also signed a "Power of Attorney," agreeing: Ping'an Light Chemical grants Xiangcai Securities the right to independently operate and manage the securities fund account opened at Xiangcai Securities' business department, with the scope of authorization including opening accounts, closing accounts, resetting passwords, freezing and unfreezing accounts, sub-accounts, Shanghai designated trading and cancellation of Shanghai designated trading, bond repurchase, repurchase designated trading and cancellation of repurchase designated trading, bond trading, stock and fund trading and placement, fund deposits, fund withdrawals, and custody transfer; the term is from April 20, 2004 to April 20, 2005. After signing the above contracts, agreements, and power of attorney, Ping'an Light Chemical transferred RMB 40 million and RMB 60 million in two separate transfers on April 20 and 21, 2004, totaling RMB 100 million to Xiangcai Securities' business department account.

Pursuant to Ping'an Light Chemical's "Notice of Transfer," Xiangcai Securities paid Ping'an Light Chemical investment returns totaling RMB 7.8 million in July 2004, October 2004, January 2005, and April 2005 respectively; in June 2005, Xiangcai Securities repaid RMB 20 million of the principal of the entrusted investment management funds.

On May 17, 2005, Xiangcai Securities issued a "Letter Regarding a Request for Extension of Repayment" to Everbright Changsha Branch, stating that the sunshine wealth management guarantee business had matured on April 20, 2005, but it was unable to perform and requested an extension for repayment.

It was further found: Xiangcai Securities is an independent enterprise legal person with registered capital of RMB 2,514,705, and its business scope includes: agency trading of securities, agency principal and interest repayment and dividend distribution, securities custody, verification, agency account registration and opening, proprietary trading of securities, securities underwriting and listing recommendation, securities investment consulting and financial advisory services, asset management, establishment of securities investment funds and fund management companies, etc.

Ping'an Light Chemical is an independent enterprise legal person with registered capital of RMB 140 million, and its shareholders are Long Dahai and Liu Wenchao.

On July 18, 2005, Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting a judgment ordering Xiangcai Securities and Ping'an Light Chemical to repay the outstanding loan of RMB 80 million and interest owed to Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch.

The court of first instance held: The "Loan Contract" signed between Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch and Ping'an Light Chemical represents the true intentions of both parties, and its content does not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations; it is a valid contract, and both parties shall strictly perform their obligations as agreed. Xiangcai Securities argued that Ping'an Light Chemical improperly channeled the loan funds into the stock market, but it provided no supporting evidence. Upon examination, Ping'an Light Chemical used all RMB 80 million of the loan to issue acceptance drafts to FAW Trading Corporation and FAW Jiefang Qingdao Automobile Factory; therefore, Xiangcai Securities' defense was inconsistent with the facts and was not accepted by the court. After signing the contract, Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch disbursed the loan as agreed, fulfilling its primary obligations under the contract. However, Ping'an Light Chemical only repaid part of the interest upon maturity and failed to fully perform its repayment obligations, thus it should bear liability for breach of contract.

Xiangcai Securities possesses the qualification for discretionary investment management approved by the regulatory authorities. The "Discretionary Investment Management Contract" and its "Supplementary Agreement" signed with Ping'an Light Chemical represent the true intentions of the parties and do not violate laws or administrative regulations prohibiting mixed operations; they should be deemed valid. However, the fixed interest set in the agreement constitutes a guaranteed floor clause, which evades and transfers investment risks, violates basic economic laws and principles of fair dealing, and contravenes provisions of China's trust and securities regulatory authorities that trust companies and entrusted investment managers shall not promise clients any returns or losses in any form; such clause is invalid. Ping'an Light Chemical cannot demand investment returns from Xiangcai Securities based on this invalid clause. The RMB 7.8 million in returns already received by Ping'an Light Chemical constitute unjust enrichment and should be returned to Xiangcai Securities.

After accepting Ping'an Light Chemical's entrustment, Xiangcai Securities should have fully managed Ping'an Light Chemical's entrusted funds as agreed, but upon expiration of the entrustment period, Xiangcai Securities failed to promptly liquidate and return the entrusted assets to Ping'an Light Chemical, thus it should bear liability for delayed payment. The "Supplementary Agreement" between Ping'an Light Chemical and Xiangcai Securities contained a clause regarding the assumption of losses, stipulating: "Upon the expiration of the management term, the agent (Xiangcai Securities) guarantees the safety and integrity of the entrusted investment management assets, ensuring the annual investment return rate of the entrusted investment management assets reaches 7.8%" and "If due to the principal's reasons... if investment losses occur, they shall be borne by the principal." The precondition for the principal to bear losses is that Xiangcai Securities must prove Ping'an Light Chemical's fault. Therefore, in the absence of evidence proving Ping'an Light Chemical's fault, Xiangcai Securities' claim for compensation for principal losses from Ping'an Light Chemical based on this clause lacks factual basis. Moreover, Xiangcai Securities itself expressly guaranteed in the "Supplementary Agreement" the safety and integrity of the entrusted assets; if losses occur, it should bear responsibility, and Ping'an Light Chemical should not bear the consequences of trading losses. Therefore, Xiangcai Securities should bear the liability for returning the principal of RMB 80 million and compensating for losses equivalent to the loan interest rate of the same period from the Bank, but the RMB 7.8 million in returns already paid by Xiangcai Securities should be offset.

During the trial, Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch clearly asserted its subrogation right against Xiangcai Securities.

Ping'an Light Chemical neither actively performed its due debt to its creditor Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch nor exercised its due claim against the secondary debtor Xiangcai Securities through necessary means; its conduct caused damage to Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch, which may exercise its subrogation right. The specific amount of the subrogated claim exercised by Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch on behalf of Ping'an Light Chemical against Xiangcai Securities as of October 21, 2004, should be RMB 84,037,496.89.

In summary, Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch's subrogation claim against Xiangcai Securities is established. Xiangcai Securities shall repay Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch the principal of RMB 80 million and interest calculated at the loan interest rate of the same period from the Bank, minus the RMB 7.8 million in returns already paid; any shortfall shall be repaid by Ping'an Light Chemical. Given that Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch did not assert its security claim against Ping'an Light Chemical, the "Pledge Contract," "Sunshine Wealth Management Guarantee Agreement," and "Letter Regarding Request for Extension of Repayment" based on the security legal relationship are not within the scope of this case and were not adjudicated. Pursuant to Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 1 and 20 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I), the court rendered the following judgment: 1. Xiangcai Securities shall pay Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch RMB 80 million in principal and interest (calculated from April 21, 2004, at the People's Bank of China's benchmark loan interest rate for the same period until the date of full payment), with the RMB 7.8 million already paid in returns offset against this amount, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect. 2. From the effective date of this judgment, the creditor-debtor relationship between Ping'an Light Chemical and Xiangcai Securities arising from the "Discretionary Investment Management Contract" in this case shall be extinguished. 3. Ping'an Light Chemical shall, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, assume repayment liability to the extent that the amount to be repaid by Xiangcai Securities under item 1 above is insufficient to satisfy Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch's debt of RMB 84,037,496.89 (interest calculated until October 21, 2004; thereafter, interest shall be calculated as stipulated in the contract until the date of full payment). Court acceptance fee of RMB 410,010 and property preservation fee of RMB 400,520, totaling RMB 810,530, shall be borne by Xiangcai Securities in the amount of RMB 730,000 and by Ping'an Light Chemical in the amount of RMB 80,530.

Dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, Xiangcai Securities appealed to this Court, alleging: Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch filed a lawsuit based on a loan contract, not a subrogation action as determined by the court of first instance; the loan contract action initiated by Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch should be dismissed. According to the principle that "no trial without complaint," the court of first instance should have only examined whether this case constituted an assumption of debt. The facts regarding subrogation are not within the scope of this case. The judgment of the court of first instance that Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch holds a claim of RMB 80 million in loan principal against Ping'an Light Chemical is unsupported by evidence, and Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch does not meet the conditions for filing a subrogation action. The court of first instance's decision ordering Xiangcai Securities to pay interest at the same-period bank loan rate to Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch was clearly improper, resulting in Ping'an Light Chemical receiving compensation far exceeding its actual losses. Due to the prolonged downturn of the stock market, the RMB 100 million entrusted by Ping'an Light Chemical for investment management had incurred losses of over RMB 33 million. Such substantial losses were not solely attributable to Xiangcai Securities' fault. The judgment of the court of first instance improperly handled the RMB 7.8 million in returns, increasing Xiangcai Securities' burden by adding bank loan interest for the same period on the RMB 7.8 million portion. Xiangcai Securities requested the court of second instance to vacate the judgment of the court of first instance, dismiss the appellee's claims, or remand the case to the court of first instance for retrial.

In response to Xiangcai Securities' appeal and reasons, Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch argued: Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch's claim against Ping'an Light Chemical is legally valid. Moreover, Ping'an Light Chemical, as the debtor under the "Loan Contract" and the creditor under the "Discretionary Investment Management Contract," after both contracts matured consecutively, neither performed its due debt to Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch nor pursued its due claim against Xiangcai Securities, which is not personal to it and involves monetary payment, through litigation or arbitration, thereby preventing the realization of Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch's due claim and causing damage. Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch naming Xiangcai Securities as defendant and Ping'an Light Chemical as third party complies with the legal provisions on exercising subrogation rights. The judgment of the court of first instance correctly determined the principal debt principal and interest as RMB 84,037,496.89, which Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch and the principal debtor Ping'an Light Chemical confirmed without error. The court of first instance, based on the creditor-debtor relationship between Xiangcai Securities and Ping'an Light Chemical, correctly determined the amount of the secondary claim as RMB 80 million plus interest at the same-period bank loan rate (deducting the RMB 7.8 million already paid by Xiangcai Securities), in line with Chinese law and judicial practice in similar cases. Therefore, the subrogation amount determined by the court of first instance based on the principal and secondary debt amounts is entirely correct. The judgment of the court of first instance has clear facts, sufficient evidence, proper handling, and lawful procedure. The appellee requested the court of second instance to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

In response to Xiangcai Securities' appeal and reasons, Ping'an Light Chemical stated: This case is a subrogation action. Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch and Ping'an Light Chemical have consistently clarified that this case is a subrogation action. Ping'an Light Chemical does not dispute the outstanding amount owed to Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch. The creditor-debtor relationship between Ping'an Light Chemical and Xiangcai Securities in equal amount shall be extinguished. For the portion of Xiangcai Securities' debt to Ping'an Light Chemical exceeding the subrogation amount claimed by Everbright Xinhua Sub-branch, Ping'an Light Chemical will pursue recovery from Xiangcai Securities through a separate lawsuit.

Upon trial in the second instance, this Court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of the Court: The Loan Contract signed between China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch and Ping An Light Chemical represented the true intent of both parties, its contents did not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and therefore it is a valid contract. After the contract was signed, China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch disbursed the loan to Ping An Light Chemical as agreed. Ping An Light Chemical was obligated to repay the full principal and interest to China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch upon maturity of the contract, and its failure to do so also triggered corresponding liability for breach of contract. Since Ping An Light Chemical had only paid partial interest to China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch, the latter was entitled to recover the outstanding principal and interest from Ping An Light Chemical and to hold it liable for the breach. China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch provided sufficient and valid evidence to prove its claim of an RMB 80,000,000 loan principal against Ping An Light Chemical, which was acknowledged by Ping An Light Chemical. Xiangcai Securities' appellate argument that the creditor-debtor relationship between China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch and Ping An Light Chemical was unclear cannot be sustained, and this Court does not support it in accordance with law.

The Entrusted Investment Management Contract and the Supplemental Agreement signed between Ping An Light Chemical as principal and Xiangcai Securities as agent provided that Ping An Light Chemical would entrust funds to Xiangcai Securities for investment in the securities market within a specified period, and Xiangcai Securities would pay corresponding investment returns to Ping An Light Chemical periodically. The above content conforms to the characteristics of an entrusted wealth management contract. The clause in which Xiangcai Securities guaranteed Ping An Light Chemical an annual investment return rate of 7.8% on its funds, with Xiangcai Securities making up any shortfall, constitutes a clause guaranteeing fixed returns on principal and interest in an entrusted wealth management contract. Article 143 of the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China clearly stipulates that securities companies shall not in any manner make promises to clients regarding the profits from securities trading or compensation for losses from securities trading. The guaranteed return clause in this case obviously violates the above prohibition under the law and should be held invalid. The guaranteed return clause is the purpose or core clause of an entrusted wealth management contract; its invalidity should render the entire entrusted wealth management contract invalid. Therefore, the Entrusted Investment Management Contract and the Supplemental Agreement in this case, being entrusted wealth management contracts, are wholly invalid. As such, Xiangcai Securities as agent shall return the full entrusted principal to Ping An Light Chemical as principal and pay interest at the fixed deposit interest rate for the corresponding period prescribed by the People's Bank of China. Ping An Light Chemical may not demand from Xiangcai Securities the investment returns stipulated in the contract; the RMB 7,800,000 it has already received shall be returned to Xiangcai Securities as unjust enrichment. The judgment of the court of first instance, which upheld the validity of the Entrusted Investment Management Contract and the Supplemental Agreement in this case and ordered Xiangcai Securities to pay interest to China Everbank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, was improper and shall be corrected.

China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch holds a creditor's right against Ping An Light Chemical, and Ping An Light Chemical holds a creditor's right against Xiangcai Securities. Both of the above creditor's rights had matured before this lawsuit was filed. Ping An Light Chemical neither performed its matured obligation to China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch nor exercised its matured creditor's right against Xiangcai Securities, thereby causing damage to China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch. China Everbright Bank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch, pursuant to Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 16, paragraph 1 of the Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, filed a request with the People's Court to subrogately exercise Ping An Light Chemical's creditor's right in its own name, which is not improper. Moreover, the amount of creditor's right that the judgment of the court of first instance determined China Everbank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch could claim against Xiangcai Securities did not exceed the amount of Ping An Light Chemical's creditor's right against Xiangcai Securities. Ping An Light Chemical raised no objection to the method or scope of China Everbank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch's claim. Therefore, Xiangcai Securities' appellate argument that China Everbank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch's right of subrogation cannot be established lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

None of the parties appealed the parts of the judgment of the court of first instance that concerned Ping An Light Chemical. Pursuant to Article 151 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court of second instance shall try the facts and applicable law relating to the appeal claims. Accordingly, this Court will not review the above parts of the judgment of the court of first instance.

In conclusion, the judgment of the court of first instance found the facts clearly, but its application of law was partially erroneous. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, subparagraphs (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby decides as follows:

1. Items 2 and 3 of the main text of the civil judgment (2005) Xiang Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 14 of the High People's Court of Hunan Province are affirmed;

2. Item 1 of the main text of the civil judgment (2005) Xiang Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 14 of the High People's Court of Hunan Province is modified as follows: Xiangcai Securities Co., Ltd. shall pay to China Everbank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch RMB 80,000,000 in principal plus interest (calculated at the fixed deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period from April 21, 2004 until the date of full payment), within 10 days after this judgment takes effect. The RMB 7,800,000 already paid shall be offset.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance and the property preservation fee shall be borne as determined in the judgment of the court of first instance. The court acceptance fee for the second instance, in the amount of RMB 410,010, shall be borne equally by Xiangcai Securities Co., Ltd. and China Everbank Changsha Xinhua Sub-branch, each in the amount of RMB 205,005.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Jin Jianfeng

Judge: Chen Bailing

Acting Judge: Yang Zhengyu

September 29, 2006

Clerk: Yuan Hongxia
